I was extremely disappointed to find out that, despite “Edited by Will Shortz” being displayed prominently on the cover, it doesn’t appear to be edited at all? Many of the puzzles are missing clues or misnumbered. Puzzle 1 in my copy has multiple impossible “clues” - 97A where there exists no 97A, or clues up to 114D where the last down clue is 112. Sadly, I had attempted and marked up the first puzzle before I realized something was wrong so I can’t return it. Checking Amazon, the reviews say this is not just a one-time misprint, but a systematic error. Sam explains TEARSHEET with: 'The term generally refers to a page torn from a magazine or journal.'
Well, yes, in the green-paintiest way possible. That would be like defining 'blue-sky' as 'like a sky that is blue', ignoring its idiomatic meaning of (perhaps foolish) optimism.  
But TEAR SHEETs have specific meanings in both finance and advertisements. Ad agencies used a page torn out of a publication as proof that the client's ad actually saw the light of print. And announcements of IPOs or extremely complex M&As would include a one-page takeaway summary of relevant financial data.
